transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. 

Um, well, I hope I'm explaining this right, and it's probably nothing too serious—maybe just getting a little older—but my wife actually suggested I come in. She's been a little frustrated with me lately, and I feel just terrible about it. She’ll be telling me about things, like my cousin’s appointments or coordinating his rides, and... well, I’m looking right at her. I really am trying to listen. But then a minute later, I realize I didn’t actually take in half of what she just said. 

I don't want her to think I'm ignoring her, because I do care. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm not wasting your time with this.
Do you often find it difficult to concentrate on conversations or tasks, even when you're trying your best to focus?

Well, yes, I suppose I do. Though I really try my best, I promise. It's not that I don't care about what I'm doing. 

Like, if I sit down to work out a catering order for an event, or if I'm listening in on a parish planning call... I always start off just fine. I'm right there, taking it all in. But then, before long, my mind just sort of... drifts? And I end up having to go back over the same notes again, almost like I never even read them in the first place. 

It's probably just a normal part of getting older, right? I mean, I'm sure everyone gets a little easily distracted sometimes. I hope that's the kind of example you were looking for?
Do you often feel restless or find yourself moving around a lot, even when you're trying to focus or when it's expected that you remain still?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I'm actually pretty good about sitting still. Like during church services or if I'm just sitting in the living room with my wife, I'm perfectly happy just staying put. I don't really get that restless feeling at all. 

I hope that's alright? I know you're probably asking for a reason, and I'd hate to mess up your evaluation, but I just don't want to make something up if it isn't there. Am I still giving you the right kind of information?
Have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even if just for a little while?

Oh, um, no... no, I wouldn't say that at all. I actually feel pretty good most days. I mean, I still really enjoy the things I do, like helping out at the parish and, you know, just spending time with my wife. I don't feel sad or down or anything like that. 

I hope it's okay that I'm saying no to that? I know you have your standard questions to get through, and I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture so I'm not making your job harder. But honestly, my mood is just fine. Is that... is that helpful?

When you think back to when you were a child, were you often easily distracted or had trouble focusing on tasks or schoolwork, or was this something that only started happening more recently as an adult?

Well, um... I suppose if I'm being completely honest, it isn't just a recent thing. I mean, I was a good kid! I never wanted to cause any trouble. But, um, even way back in grade school, definitely before I was twelve, my teachers used to tell my parents that I was... well, they said I was a bright boy, which was very kind of them to say. 

But they also mentioned that I was always daydreaming. I'd accidentally leave my completed homework just sitting inside my desk, or I'd need a few extra reminders from the teacher to actually finish my classwork. It wasn't that I was trying to be lazy or disobedient, I promise. My head was just sort of in the clouds back then, too. 

Does that help at all? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of background for your notes. I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.

To better understand the pattern of your difficulties with focus, can you confirm whether these issues with being easily distracted or not completing tasks were present before you turned 12 years old?

Yes, um, I believe I just mentioned that... I hope I didn't confuse things by bringing it up too early? But yes, absolutely, it was definitely before I turned 12. Like I was saying, back in grade school, my teachers would always tell my parents that I was a bright boy, but that I was just daydreaming a lot. 

I'd do the homework, I really would, but then I'd just leave it sitting right there in my desk. And they'd have to give me little reminders to finish whatever we were working on in class. I really tried my best to be a good student, though. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be sure I'm answering exactly what you need for your evaluation.
